# Results — Study 825 (Oil Predicts Equities)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Driesprong, Jacobsen & Maat (2008), "Striking Oil: Another Puzzle?": a rise in the oil
price **this month** predicts **lower** equity returns **next month** (oil as a
slow-diffusing macro shock), so the predictive slope of SPY's forward one-month return on
the trailing one-month oil return should be **negative**. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Stamped as-of 2026-06-30
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `effe48bc1a4f` (panel SPY close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted close (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **USO** (crude-oil ETF) + **SPY** (S&P 500 ETF), 2006-04-10 → 2026-06-30, **5,087** aligned daily rows |
| Resample | month-end (`ME`) last close → monthly simple returns; **241** monthly observations (2006-05-31 → 2026-05-31) |
| Signal | the **trailing one-month oil (USO) return** known at the close of month `t` (the predictor `x`) |
| Target | the **forward one-month equity (SPY) return** over month `t+1` (`equity.shift(-1)`, the target `y`) |
| Regression | single-regressor OLS `y = α + β·x + ε`; the Driesprong slope `β` (monthly SPY return per unit monthly oil return) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: oil return through close `t` → hold SPY over month `t+1`. The costed timer trades `−sign(oil_ret)` of SPY, one-way cost × NAV per rebalance leg, 50 bps/yr borrow on shorts |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the slope; OLS *t*; R²; a Welch tercile cross-check; a 2,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** USO and SPY are continuously-listed liquid
ETFs, so there is **no delisting bias** on this pair; the caveat is instead that USO (a
front-month roll vehicle with well-documented contango drag) is an **ETF proxy** for the
oil price, not the spot or a constant-maturity index — a signal-construction choice, not a
survivorship one.

## The headline — the predictive regression

`r_equity[t+1] = α + β·r_oil[t]` on n = **241** months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **slope β (Driesprong coefficient)** | **+0.0136** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* on β | **+0.33** |
| OLS *t* on β | +0.52 |
| R² | **0.11%** |
| α (intercept) | +0.99%/mo |
| next-month SPY after oil **fell** (bottom tercile) | +0.95% |
| next-month SPY after oil **rose** (top tercile) | +0.83% (Welch *t* = −0.15) |

The claimed edge **does not replicate.** Driesprong et al predict a *negative* slope
(oil up → stocks down next month); on this 2006–2026 tape the slope is **+0.0136** with a
Newey-West *t* of just **+0.33** and an R² of **0.11%** — statistically indistinguishable
from zero, and if anything the *wrong* (positive) sign. Next-month SPY is essentially the
same whether oil rose or fell the month before. There is no predictive content here.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) slope even a lucky alignment?

Keep the predictor `x`, permute the target `y` (predictor → target link broken), 2,000 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | **+0.0136** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.0002 (0.0260) |
| two-sided p (|β| ≥ observed) | **0.587** |

The observed slope sits comfortably inside the permutation null — p = 0.59, i.e. pure
noise. Nothing to explain.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-01-01)

| era | n | slope β | NW *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2006-01 → 2016-01 | 116 | +0.0689 | +1.23 | 2.15% |
| 2016-01 → 2026-06 | 125 | −0.0234 | −0.50 | 0.41% |

The slope not only stays insignificant in both halves — it **flips sign** across eras.
Whatever transient co-movement existed in the crisis-heavy first decade (weakly *positive*,
still the wrong sign for Driesprong) is gone in the second. No stable relation.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Trade `−sign(oil_ret[t])` of SPY over month `t+1`; one-way cost × NAV per rebalance leg,
50 bps/yr borrow on shorts. Benchmarked against simply holding SPY.

| book | net/mo | *t* | Sharpe | ~ann. | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| long/short, 1 bp | +0.170% | +0.58 | 0.13 | +2.0% | hit rate 0.506 — a coin flip |
| long/short, 5 bps | +0.132% | +0.45 | 0.10 | +1.6% | — |
| long/flat, 1 bp | +0.593% | +2.60 | 0.58 | +7.1% | *inherits the equity premium* |
| **SPY buy & hold** | **+0.973%** | **+3.44** | **0.77** | — | the long/flat timer **loses to this** |

The long/short book is a coin flip (hit rate 0.506, *t* = 0.58). The long/flat variant
*looks* significant (*t* = 2.60) — but only because being long SPY roughly half the time
harvests the equity risk premium, **not** any oil signal; it earns a **lower** Sharpe
(0.58) than just buying and holding SPY (0.77). The oil forecast subtracts value. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded daily tape where the equity month-`t+1` return loads on the oil
month-`t` return with slope `−edge` (Driesprong direction). No network.

| world | slope NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.01** (sd 1.03), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (≈ the nominal 5%) |
| planted (`edge = 0.35`, seed 825) | β = **−0.1951**, ***t* = −5.91**, R² = 12.40% |

The regression recovers a *planted* negative Driesprong slope cleanly and fires on the null
at only the nominal rate — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine null, not a broken
engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The celebrated Driesprong negative oil→equity predictive slope does
  **not** replicate on 2006–2026 US ETFs. The slope is **+0.0136** (Newey-West *t* =
  **+0.33**, R² = **0.11%**) — flat, and if anything the *wrong* (positive) sign versus the
  claimed negative one; p = 0.59 in a 2,000-draw placebo; it flips sign across eras
  (*t* = +1.23 / −0.50). A 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* negative slope
  cleanly, so the null is real. The claimed edge is absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long/short timer is a coin flip (net +0.17%/mo, *t* = 0.58,
  hit 0.506). The long/flat variant only *looks* positive because it inherits the equity
  premium — and it still earns a lower Sharpe (0.58) than buying and holding SPY (0.77). No
  paycheck.
